messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 detected — KV cache working set spike + continuous-batching backpressure in us-east-1. Symptoms: 10x batch wait times, scheduler fairness skew, tail latency spikes. Incident ID INC-2026-0315-01. Please ack and join #incidents.

maya: acked. I'm looking at kvcache metrics now, seeing eviction rate jumped ~12x at 13:42 UTC. Memory at 91% on kvpool-3.

jorge: on it. uploading a quick diagnostic: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/kvcache?pool=kvpool-3 | jq '.evictions, .mem_pct, .hot_keys[0:5]'` shows heavy hot-key churn from a small set of long-context requests. We have a lot of mixed long/short requests causing batch scheduler to favor long ones -> starvation.

liam: confirmed from batch-scheduler side: backlog for short requests has queues >200ms wait, p90 generation latency up 2.8x. See flamechart: short requests stuck behind large KV loads in the scheduler's priority bucket.

elaine: cs-ops, heads-up: several customers on dedicated have reported slow responses (tickets #1321, #1324). Not mass outage but degraded for some routes.

maya: hypothesis: recent default batch_window increase from 6ms -> 20ms (deployed last night) combined with kv prefix caching causing excessive KV prefetch/pinning -> cache blowup.

jorge: reproduction locally with a mixed workload shows continuous batching holding large KV pages in memory while long requests keep large KV contexts pinned. Patch idea: 1) temporarily lower `batch_window_ms` to 6ms, 2) disable `prefix_cache_prefetch` for affected pools, 3) increase kvpool replica count by +1 to relieve pressure.

maya: I'm going to apply the first two config toggles as an emergency mitigation. If that looks stable we'll scale. Going to run the rollout in canary on kvpool-3.

eng-runtime: FYI deploy bot will report rollout. Make sure to use `--canary=10%` and `--max-unavailable=0` for safety.

maya: executing now: ```
# emergency mitigation
kubectl set env deploy/kv-runtime batch_window_ms=6 --namespace=prod-us-east-1
kubectl patch cm kvpool-config -p '{"data":{"prefix_cache_prefetch":"false"}}' -n prod-us-east-1
```

deploy-bot: Started rollout for deploy/kv-runtime in prod-us-east-1 (canary 10%). Correlation ID: dpl-6a7b.

maya: canary metrics look good at 2 minutes: eviction rate dropped ~70% on canary nodes, short request wait decreased. Rolling to 50%.

liam: telemetry: p99 for short requests down from 3.2s -> 750ms on rolled nodes. BUT overall cluster still has some hot shards with mem above 88%.

maya: scaling kvpool-3 by +1 now: `kubectl scale statefulset/kvpool-3 --replicas=5 -n prod-us-east-1`

deploy-bot: Scale started for statefulset/kvpool-3.

jorge: also adding a temporary scheduler fairness tweak: lower max_batch_tokens for long requests to 50% of default to prevent long requests blocking the queue. Patching scheduler config now.

maya: applied scheduler patch and rolled it to prod. Observed immediate drop in long-request head-of-line blocking.

cs-ops: Customer update drafted: "We're investigating elevated latencies for some requests; mitigation underway. No data loss. We'll share updates in 30 minutes." Shall I push?

elaine: push now, add impacted customers list (IDs in ticket). Set statuspage to degraded perf for specific API routes.

cs-ops: done — statuspage updated, customers notified.

liam: monitoring for 15m stable window: eviction rate trending down cluster-wide, queues for short requests under 20ms again on most nodes. Some leftover shards still recovering.

maya: marking current mitigation as partial mitigation. Need follow-ups: 1) postmortem, 2) revert last night's batch_window change after analysis, 3) add workload-aware batch_window defaults, 4) automated hotspot breaker that prevents prefix prefetch if mem >85%.

eng-runtime: LGTM on follow-ups. Also recommend we add a scheduler fairness test in CI that mixes long/short request traces.

oncall-bot: @maya you have scheduled handoff in 25 minutes to @jorge (next oncall). Please summarize next steps and open a follow-up ticket.

maya: summary for handoff: mitigation applied (batch_window->6ms, prefix prefetch disabled, +1 replica, scheduler max_batch_tokens reduced for long requests). Cluster stable but some shards in warm recovery. Active tasks: postmortem (PM-INC-230), add emergency guard for prefetch memory threshold, revert/validate last night's config change. Handing to @jorge at 14:10 UTC.

jorge: acked. I'll own the follow-ups and will shepherd the postmortem. Will also own communication for any potential rollbacks.

cs-ops: thanks — we'll keep customers updated with final incident summary and ETA for fixes.

maya: quick note — we've saved a heap profile and kvcache snapshots (s3://redwood-logs/inc-1769923456/) for postmortem.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete. New oncall: @jorge. Incident remains open (severity degraded) until postmortem and config rollback plan are complete.

eli: (outside thread) nice containment work, team. :thumbsup:
